## Context / Problem

At audited code snapshot `9a94ef9737fbdf070ae314bba6e797319aee2301`,
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py:1-800` and
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py:1-800` are exactly at the locked
800-line module-size cap. Any net addition fails the existing CI gate. Brant's existing
`wormlike-buried-grunion` prerequisite restores headroom in `run_differs.py`,
`outbound_differ.py`, and `applier.py`; it deliberately does not own these two spine modules.

The prior RP-03 work made `reconcile_once` a thin lifecycle sequencer over existing load, diff,
apply, and persist phases and introduced the current per-pass state carrier. Preserve that decision.
The pre-observation repair boundary from ADR 0099 is load-bearing: repair remains after the
under-lock staleness check and before the first remote fetch.

Provenance: janitor finding S14 (validity 0.90, impact 1.00), discovered during
`literal-subaverage-dartfrog`. This story restores optionality needed by Brant; it does not add
typed-payload behavior.

## Approach / End State

- Re-measure both modules against the current Brant prerequisite tip before editing and record the
  baseline.
- Restore real headroom through deletion or extraction of cohesive phase-owned call-graph clusters.
  Current candidate seams are `_load_snapshots`, `_apply_mutations`, `_persist_and_log`, and
  their existing helper families; use the contract story's final ownership decision if it changes
  those seams.
- Keep `reconcile_once` as the lifecycle facade and reuse the existing pass state. Do not introduce
  a second generic pass/ticket context or move unrelated behavior merely to reduce a number.
- Preserve public/import/monkeypatch compatibility only where the census proves a supported
  consumer. Re-anchor structural tests when a symbol legitimately moves rather than retaining a
  compatibility cycle.
- Preserve the ADR 0099 repair ordering with a behavioral oracle that is proven to fail when repair
  moves after observation.

`cascade_flag=true`: these modules are high-centrality orchestration surfaces. Census semantic
callers plus string/dynamic references, including monkeypatch, `getattr`, importlib, file-path
loading, complexity-baseline keys, and structural tests.

## Sequencing

This story follows `scummy-ultrashort-tuatara` so the accepted payload/producer contract fixes the
ownership boundary, runs in parallel with the disjoint `wormlike-buried-grunion` extraction, and
must close before `earthborn-statuelike-boutu` adds typed-payload implementation.

## Testing

Use the existing reconciler orchestration and recovery-boundary suites unchanged except for
necessary import/structural re-anchors. Run the module-size and complexity gates, lint, typecheck,
and the focused reconciler suite. Seed a post-fetch repair move and observe the ordering test fail
before restoring the correct order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The pre-change baseline is recorded against the current prerequisite tip; if either cited
      module was already brought below 700 lines, no replacement work is invented for that module.
- [x] `reconcile.py` and `reconcile_helpers.py` are each at or below 700 lines on the completed
      tree, without changing the locked 800-line limit.
- [x] Every new module is at least 100 lines and represents a cohesive existing call-graph cluster;
      no split is mechanical and resulting modules follow the 200-500 LOC target where practicable.
- [x] `reconcile_once` remains the single lifecycle facade and no second generic pass/ticket
      context or duplicate operation authority is introduced.
- [x] Repair remains after `ensure_selection_current` and before the first remote fetch; the
      behavioral oracle is demonstrated RED under a seeded post-fetch move and GREEN after restore.
- [x] Semantic references and a repository string/dynamic-reference sweep are recorded for every
      moved symbol, and supported monkeypatch/import surfaces continue to resolve without a cycle.
- [x] Existing reconciler behavior is unchanged: focused orchestration/recovery suites pass without
      weakened assertions, and Brant's portable parity corpus remains green once available.
- [x] Module-size, complexity-ratchet, lint, and typecheck gates pass with no limit or baseline
      increase.

## Completion evidence

- Baseline (worktree tip): reconcile.py=800, reconcile_helpers.py=800 lines.
  Final: reconcile.py=333, reconcile_helpers.py=394, pass_support.py=464,
  load_phase.py=260, apply_phase.py=192, persist_phase.py=301 lines.
- Semantic (Serena) + string/monkeypatch/dynamic-reference census recorded
  per moved symbol; two real non-test consumers of resolve_selection/
  SelectionError (`_lib_ops.py`, `__main__.py`) were found outside
  reconcile.py's re-export shim and re-pointed at pass_support.py.
- ADR 0099 repair-ordering behavioral oracle
  (`test_repair_runs_before_the_first_remote_observation`) demonstrated
  RED (events=['remote-fetch','repair']) under a seeded post-fetch repair
  move, then GREEN after restoring the correct order.
- AC7 parity-corpus clause: Brant's portable parity corpus
  (`wormlike-buried-grunion`) had not landed in this worktree at completion
  time; this clause is deferred per the plan-review's own advisory finding
  (id fd50f3f3d0ca1362a) and is not required for this story's closure since
  the corpus is a disjoint, parallel prerequisite this story does not own.
- Gates: make lint, make typecheck, module-size contract test, and
  `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` (new=0 increased=0) all green.
  Full `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` (3651 passed) and the broader
  reconciler-adjacent suites (contracts, interfaces, integration, scripts)
  green. Landed as Gerrit change 2409 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, MERGED,
  commit ff484948488f).
